zh.summary: 分辨 DNS 解析與網域註冊資料，以可查核的線索建立足跡，不把服務商誤當擁有人。

sourceBody.text: M02-04｜DNS、WHOIS / RDAP Footprinting：查得到地址，不等於知道屋主
1｜結論先行：把「服務怎麼找到」與「網域怎麼登記」分開
今天只學一個完整概念：用 DNS 與網域註冊資料建立可查證的外部輪廓，而不是看到一個 IP 就認定找到公司的主機或擁有人。
DNS（Domain Name System，網域名稱系統）像電話簿加分層問路系統，回答「這個名稱有哪些服務紀錄」。WHOIS（傳統註冊資料查詢協定）與 RDAP（Registration Data Access Protocol，註冊資料存取協定）則比較像查登記資料，回答「這個網域在註冊體系中留下哪些資料」。Footprinting（足跡蒐集）是把這些線索整理成範圍清楚、附時間與來源的輪廓。
生活上，一間咖啡店的外送聯絡電話、代收郵件地址、店面租約登記人可能各不相同。網域也一樣：網站、信箱、DNS 託管商、註冊商和實際營運者可以是不同角色。真正要學會的是「每個欄位回答哪個問題，以及不能回答什麼」。
2｜DNS 查詢的旅程：誰幫你問，誰有權回答？
假設你要開啟合成案例的 www.coffee.example。你的裝置通常先問遞迴解析器（Recursive Resolver）：一個替你找答案、也可能保存先前答案的服務。若快取已有可使用的答案，它就回覆，不必每次從頭找。
若需要查找，解析器可沿 DNS 階層取得指引：根名稱伺服器知道頂層網域的委派資訊；頂層網域（Top-Level Domain，TLD）伺服器再指向相關網域的權威名稱伺服器（Authoritative Name Server）。權威伺服器提供它負責區域的紀錄。這是角色示意，不代表每次查詢都會走完整條路。
「遞迴」是幫你完成查找；「權威」是對自己管理的區域提供正式資料。DNS 區域（Zone）是一段由特定權威伺服器管理的名稱空間，與口語中的整個網域不一定完全重合，子網域可以另外委派。以上角色與委派結構可參考 [RFC 1034](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034)。
快取（Cache）像抄下來暫時使用的電話簿。TTL（Time to Live，存活時間）告訴快取一筆紀錄可以保留多久；它不是「修改後全世界一定在這個時間內更新」的保證。觀察到的 TTL 也可能是剩餘時間。不同解析器、查詢時間或網路位置，可能看到不同結果。

sourceBody.text: 3｜讀懂紀錄：每種欄位都只回答自己的問題
資源紀錄（Resource Record）是 DNS 中的資料單位。不要把所有紀錄都解讀成「這是公司的伺服器」。

rows: A
名稱對應 IPv4 位址
可能是共用主機或代理服務，不一定是原始主機
AAAA
名稱對應 IPv6 位址
與 A 分開查；沒有 A 不代表沒有服務
CNAME
這個名稱是另一個名稱的別名
可看出服務依賴，但不能直接斷言最終主機歸屬
MX
郵件應送往哪些郵件交換主機
是收信路由線索，不代表每封信的寄件來源
NS
這個區域由哪些名稱伺服器服務
常反映 DNS 託管，不等於網域擁有人
SOA
區域管理的起始資訊與計時參數
序號協助區域版本管理，不保證是日期格式
TXT
文字資料，可供驗證或政策使用
要依內容與相應規格解讀，不是看到文字就當秘密
PTR
常用於反向查詢，由位址找名稱
不是法律上的所有權證明，也不保證與正向查詢一一對應

sourceBody.text: MX 的偏好值較小者優先嘗試，不是較大者更重要。TXT 可能放 SPF（Sender Policy Framework，寄信來源政策）、網域驗證字串等；這些用途不同，不能混為「所有 TXT 都是郵件設定」。DNS 的基本紀錄格式及多數上述類型見 [RFC 1035](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035)；IPv6 的 AAAA 紀錄見 [RFC 3596](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3596)。

items.body: 分清位址、別名、郵件與區域角色，不推論所有權。

sourceBody.text: 4｜WHOIS 與 RDAP：註冊商不是註冊人
註冊人（Registrant）是網域註冊關係中的持有人角色；註冊商（Registrar）提供網域註冊服務；註冊管理機構（Registry）管理某個頂層網域的登錄資料。這三者不是同一件事。即使某平台同時提供多種服務，仍要按欄位角色判讀。
傳統 WHOIS 使用 TCP（Transmission Control Protocol，傳輸控制協定）的 43 埠；埠可想成服務的收件窗口。回覆常是文字，格式及可取得的欄位會因服務而異；協定本身沒有內建強固的存取控制或資料保密機制。[RFC 3912](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3912)
RDAP 的安全規範要求支援 HTTPS，也就是以加密連線傳送 HTTP（Hypertext Transfer Protocol，超文字傳輸協定，網頁傳輸常用規則）資料；但連線安全仍不代表每個登記欄位都能證實網站實際營運者。[RFC 7481](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7481)
RDAP 使用標準化查詢與結構化回應，讓人和程式較容易辨識欄位；JSON（JavaScript Object Notation，資料交換格式）就是把欄位名稱和值組織起來的方式，不是網頁畫面本身。RDAP 回應可包含名稱、狀態、事件、實體及其角色、名稱伺服器、說明與連結，應連同角色和事件類型一起讀。[RFC 9083](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9083)
例如「某日期」要先看它是註冊、更新還是到期事件；更新日期不等於網站改版日，註冊日期不等於公司成立日。顯示某註冊商，也不等於網站由該註冊商營運。資料因隱私保護而遮蔽或缺省時，結論是「公開資料不足」，不是「沒有持有人」或「一定可疑」。
截至本課查核，ICANN 說明 RDAP 已成為註冊資料的主要替代協定；自 2025 年 1 月 28 日起，一般頂層網域的註冊管理機構與註冊商通常不再被要求提供 WHOIS，但頁面列有 .com、.name、.post 例外。這不是所有 WHOIS 已消失，也不能直接套用到所有國家或地區頂層網域。[ICANN RDAP 說明](https://www.icann.org/rdap)

sourceBody.text: 內容傳遞網路（Content Delivery Network，CDN）或反向代理（Reverse Proxy，替後端接收請求的前端服務）可能讓你只看見對外入口，而看不見原始主機。多個網站共用一個入口 IP 很常見；共用 IP 不代表同一家公司。這裡的安全做法是把關係寫成「觀察到依賴或對應」，而非「已證實資產歸屬」。
6｜查不到、查不同，以及被動／主動的界線
NXDOMAIN 表示回覆中指出所問名稱不存在；沒有某一種紀錄，不一定是名稱不存在。逾時則是沒有及時收到答案，可能與網路、伺服器、限制或設定有關，不能寫成「不存在」。務必保留回應狀態、查詢名稱和類型，而不是只抄一個空白結果。DNS 負面回覆也可能被快取。[RFC 2308](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308)
結果不同，可能是快取、變更時點、地理或負載導向、不同 DNS 視圖。Split DNS（分割視圖 DNS）讓內外部網路看到不同答案，因此外部沒看到某主機，不能推論內部沒有。也不能憑兩次結果不同就宣告 DNS 被竄改。
查第三方已保存的歷史 DNS 資料，和直接向解析器或權威伺服器查詢，不是同一種互動。一般 DNS 查詢仍會產生網路流量；你問遞迴解析器，也可能間接觸發它去問權威伺服器。是否列為被動蒐集，要按課程定義與書面測試規則判斷，不能拿「DNS 是公開的」當作不限量或不限對象的授權。
本單元重點是少量、範圍明確的紀錄判讀。先前 M04 的 DNS Enumeration（DNS 列舉）內容可用來快速複習：蒐集單筆線索，不等於已列出所有名稱；大量猜名稱、測試區域傳送或進一步探測，都要另外確認授權與規則，不在本課執行。
7｜防護與證據：看得見，不等於可任意存取
DNS 本來就需要對外公布部分服務線索。防護目標不是把一切藏起來，而是讓公開資料恰當、管理權安全、服務本身有存取控制。
可落實的作法包括定期盤點公開紀錄，移除不再使用的紀錄與服務依賴，避免把內部命名或敏感資料放入公開區域，保護註冊商與 DNS 管理帳號，啟用適當的多因素驗證與異動監控。若 CNAME 指向已停用的外部服務，先核實服務實際狀態與可接管條件，再處理紀錄，不能僅靠名稱就宣布可接管。
DNSSEC（Domain Name System Security Extensions，DNS 安全擴充）讓驗證端檢查 DNS 資料來源真實性及完整性。它不會把 DNS 內容加密，也不保證網站內容安全、服務不中斷或網域營運者可信；這幾種安全問題必須分開處理。[RFC 4033](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033)

rows: 範圍與來源
被授權的名稱、查詢服務或資料庫、直接查詢或歷史資料
時間與條件
日期、時區、解析器、網路視角、查詢名稱與紀錄類型
原始結果
回應狀態、紀錄值、TTL；只保留必要資料
判讀
觀察到的事實、可能解釋、尚未證實的歸屬
防護核驗
經授權的變更前後比較、管理紀錄及仍待確認之處

sourceBody.text: 8｜小檢核：一個情境，四個判讀
在授權的合成練習中，你看到：www.coffee.example 指向某 CDN 名稱；A 回覆 192.0.2.10；RDAP 只有註冊商資料，持有人欄位未公開；另一位同事的 DNS 查詢逾時。
請試著用自己的話回答：① 可以把 192.0.2.10 當成咖啡店專屬原始主機嗎？② 註冊商能直接當成網站擁有人嗎？③ 逾時能當成名稱不存在嗎？④ 若想讓報告可重查，你最少要補哪些查詢條件？
這是理解檢核，不需要實際操作第三方目標。未作答只代表尚未取得理解證據，不會因此標記已學會。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：CDN 位址不是原始主機證明
paragraphs: 不能。A 紀錄只顯示這次解析取得的位址；CDN 可能代理多個網站。沒有足夠證據證實它專屬咖啡店，更不能因此把整個 CDN 納入授權範圍。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：角色不同，不能互換
paragraphs: 不能。註冊商是提供網域註冊服務的角色，不必然是網站營運者。持有人資料未公開時，應記錄公開資料不足，不猜測姓名或所有權。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：逾時不是不存在
paragraphs: 不能。逾時表示沒有及時收到回應，可能與網路或服務狀態有關；NXDOMAIN 才是回覆所述的名稱不存在狀態。即使收到 NXDOMAIN，也須留下來源、時間及查詢條件。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：讓另一個人能照條件重查
paragraphs: 至少保留授權範圍、查詢日期與時區、來源或解析器、網路視角、完整名稱、紀錄類型、回應狀態及原始值。若有 TTL 也一併記錄，並將「觀察」與「尚未證實的歸屬」分開。

sourceBody.text: 9｜今天帶走的觀念與來源
一句話收束：DNS 告訴你「名稱如何連到服務」，WHOIS／RDAP 告訴你「註冊資料如何描述角色」；兩者都需要來源、時間與限制，才能變成可靠的資產線索。
下一個單元是 M02-05 Email Footprinting，再把郵件線索接回寄送路徑與可證實的資訊。這裡不先增加另一個單元。

主要查證來源：[DNS 概念 RFC 1034](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034)、[DNS 紀錄 RFC 1035](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035)、[IPv6 DNS RFC 3596](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3596)、[負面快取 RFC 2308](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308)、[RDAP JSON RFC 9083](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9083)、[ICANN RDAP](https://www.icann.org/rdap)、[DNSSEC RFC 4033](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033)。

en.summary: Distinguish DNS resolution from registration data and build an evidence-based footprint without mistaking providers for owners.

sourceBody.text: M02-04 | DNS, WHOIS / RDAP Footprinting: An Address Does Not Identify the Owner
1 | The main idea: Separate finding a service from registering a domain
Today we study one complete concept: using DNS and domain registration data to build a verifiable external picture, rather than assuming that an IP address identifies a company's server or owner.

DNS, the Domain Name System, works like a telephone directory combined with a layered system for asking directions. It answers, “What service records exist for this name?” WHOIS, the traditional registration-data query protocol, and RDAP, the Registration Data Access Protocol, are closer to looking up registration records. They answer, “What information does the registration system hold about this domain?” Footprinting means organizing these clues into a clearly scoped picture with sources and timestamps.

Think of a coffee shop. Its delivery telephone number, mail-receiving address, and the person named on its lease may all differ. Domains are similar: the website, email service, DNS hosting provider, registrar, and actual operator can involve different roles. The important skill is knowing which question each field answers—and which questions it does not answer.
2 | The DNS lookup journey: Who asks for you, and who can answer authoritatively?

Suppose you want to open www.coffee.example in our fictional scenario. Your device normally asks a recursive resolver first. This service finds answers for you and may also keep previous answers. If its cache already contains a usable answer, it can reply without starting the search again.

When a lookup is needed, the resolver can follow referrals through the DNS hierarchy. Root name servers provide delegation information for top-level domains. A Top-Level Domain, or TLD, server then points toward the domain's authoritative name servers. An authoritative server supplies records for the zone it serves. This describes the roles; it does not mean every query follows the entire path.

“Recursive” means completing the lookup on your behalf. “Authoritative” means supplying authoritative data for a zone the server manages. A DNS zone is a portion of the namespace managed by particular authoritative servers. It does not always match the whole domain as people use that word in conversation: a subdomain can be delegated separately. See [RFC 1034](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034) for these roles and delegation concepts.

A cache resembles a copied telephone directory that remains usable temporarily. TTL, or Time to Live, tells a cache how long it may retain a record. It does not guarantee that every system worldwide will reflect a change within that period. The TTL you observe may also be the remaining lifetime. Different resolvers, query times, or network locations can produce different results.

visual.description: A device asks a resolver; delegation leads to authoritative data when needed.

items.body: A device asks a resolver; delegation leads to authoritative data when needed.

sourceBody.text: 3 | Reading records: Each type answers its own question
A resource record is a unit of data in DNS. Do not interpret every record as saying, “This is the company's server.”

rows: A
Maps a name to an IPv4 address
May identify shared hosting or a proxy, not necessarily an origin server
AAAA
Maps a name to an IPv6 address
Query separately from A; no A record does not mean no service
CNAME
Makes one name an alias for another name
Can reveal a service dependency, but does not establish ownership of the final server
MX
Identifies mail exchange hosts to which mail should be sent
A clue about incoming-mail routing, not the source of every outgoing message
NS
Identifies name servers serving a zone
Often reflects DNS hosting, not the domain holder
SOA
Provides zone administration information and timing parameters
Its serial helps track zone versions; it is not guaranteed to use a date format
TXT
Holds text used for purposes such as verification or policy
Interpret its content under the relevant specification; text is not automatically a secret
PTR
Commonly supports reverse lookup, from an address to a name
Not legal proof of ownership, nor a guarantee of a one-to-one match with forward lookup

sourceBody.text: For MX records, a lower preference number is tried first; a higher number does not mean greater importance. TXT records may contain SPF, the Sender Policy Framework used to express sending-source policy, or domain-verification strings. These serve different purposes: not every TXT record is an email setting. See [RFC 1035](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035) for basic record formats and most of the types above, and [RFC 3596](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3596) for IPv6 AAAA records.

sourceBody.text: 4 | WHOIS and RDAP: A registrar is not a registrant

A registrant is the holder role in a domain registration relationship. A registrar provides domain registration services. A registry maintains registration information for a top-level domain. These are distinct roles. Even when a platform offers several services, interpret each field according to its stated role.

Traditional WHOIS uses TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) port 43. A port is a service endpoint, like a receiving window for that service. Its responses are often text, with formatting and available fields varying by service. The protocol itself has no built-in strong access-control or data-confidentiality mechanisms. [RFC 3912](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3912)

RDAP security requirements mandate support for HTTPS, which carries HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol, a commonly used set of rules for web transfers) data over an encrypted connection. A secure connection does not, however, make every registration field proof of the website’s actual operator. [RFC 7481](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7481)

RDAP uses standardized queries and structured responses, making fields easier for people and software to identify. JSON, or JavaScript Object Notation, is a data-exchange format that organizes field names and values; it is not the web page's visual presentation. An RDAP response may include names, status, events, entities and their roles, name servers, notices, and links. Read roles and event types together with their values. [RFC 9083](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9083)

For example, before interpreting a date, check whether its event is registration, update, or expiration. An update date is not necessarily the date of a website redesign; a registration date is not a company's incorporation date. A listed registrar does not mean that registrar operates the website. If privacy protection causes fields to be redacted or omitted, the conclusion is “insufficient public information,” not “there is no holder” or “this must be suspicious.”

At the time of this lesson's check, ICANN describes RDAP as the principal replacement protocol for registration data. Since January 28, 2025, generic top-level domain registries and registrars generally have no obligation to provide WHOIS, but the page lists exceptions for .com, .name, and .post. This does not mean every WHOIS service has disappeared, and it should not be applied automatically to every country-code top-level domain. [ICANN's RDAP explanation](https://www.icann.org/rdap)

sourceBody.text: 5 | Connecting the clues: An external picture of a fictional coffee shop
All data below was invented for teaching; it is not an actual query result. The .example names and documentation IP address are illustrations, not targets for testing third parties.

rows: The CNAME for www.coffee.example points to edge.vendor.example
This website name aliases another name
Its origin server belongs to that provider, or the provider's entire infrastructure is authorized for testing
A subsequent A response for the alias is 192.0.2.10
This lookup returned that IPv4 address
The IP is exclusive to the coffee shop, identifies its internal network, or has a vulnerability
The MX for coffee.example is 10 mail.vendor.example
Incoming-mail routing points to that mail host
You have obtained the account list, sender identities, or passwords
RDAP identifies an example registrar in the registrar role
The registration data assigns that registrar role
The example registrar is the shop owner
A query at another time returns a different IP
Results differ; preserve both timestamps and query conditions
A compromise definitely occurred

sourceBody.text: A Content Delivery Network, or CDN, or a reverse proxy—a front-end service receiving requests on behalf of a back end—may expose only a public entry point rather than the origin server. Several websites commonly share one entry-point IP. A shared IP does not mean the sites belong to the same company. Describe the relationship as an “observed dependency or mapping,” not “confirmed asset ownership.”
6 | Missing and different answers, and the passive/active boundary

NXDOMAIN means the response states that the queried name does not exist. The absence of one record type does not necessarily mean the name is absent. A timeout means no answer arrived in time; causes may involve the network, server, restrictions, or configuration. Do not report it as “does not exist.” Preserve the response status, query name, and query type instead of recording only a blank result. Negative DNS responses may also be cached. [RFC 2308](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308)

Different results may reflect caching, the timing of changes, geographic or load-based routing, or different DNS views. Split DNS provides different answers to internal and external networks. Therefore, not seeing a host externally does not prove it is absent internally. Two different answers alone also do not establish DNS tampering.

Looking at historical DNS data already held by a third party is a different interaction from querying a resolver or authoritative server directly. An ordinary DNS query still generates network traffic. Asking a recursive resolver can indirectly cause it to query an authoritative server. Whether an activity counts as passive collection depends on the course definition and written testing rules. “DNS is public” is not authorization for unlimited queries or unrestricted targets.

This unit focuses on interpreting a small number of clearly scoped records. Use the earlier M04 material on DNS Enumeration—systematically discovering DNS information—as a brief review: collecting one clue does not mean you have listed every name. Large-scale name guessing, zone-transfer testing, or further probing require separate confirmation of authorization and rules; we do not perform them in this lesson.
7 | Protection and evidence: Visibility does not grant unrestricted access

DNS needs to publish some service information. The defensive goal is not to hide everything. It is to keep public information appropriate, management access secure, and the services themselves protected by access controls.

Practical measures include regularly reviewing public records, removing unused records and service dependencies, keeping internal naming and sensitive information out of public zones, protecting registrar and DNS administration accounts, and enabling suitable multifactor authentication and change monitoring. If a CNAME points to a discontinued external service, verify the service's actual state and the conditions required for takeover before addressing the record. A name alone does not prove that takeover is possible.

DNSSEC, Domain Name System Security Extensions, lets a validating party check DNS data's origin authenticity and integrity. It does not encrypt DNS content or guarantee safe website content, uninterrupted service, or a trustworthy domain operator. These are separate security questions. [RFC 4033](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033)

rows: Scope and source
Authorized name, query service or database, and whether the data came from a direct query or historical records
Time and conditions
Date, time zone, resolver, network viewpoint, query name, and record type
Original result
Response status, record values, and TTL; retain only necessary data
Interpretation
Observed facts, possible explanations, and ownership that remains unverified
Defensive validation
Authorized before-and-after comparisons, administration records, and remaining uncertainties

sourceBody.text: For example, “the old CNAME was removed” needs support from the configuration change and appropriate checks. If a cache still returns the old value immediately after a change, examine timing, TTL, and the query source before declaring the change unsuccessful.

sourceBody.text: 8 | Small check: One scenario, four interpretations

In an authorized fictional exercise, you observe that www.coffee.example points to a CDN name. An A response returns 192.0.2.10. RDAP provides registrar information but does not publicly disclose the holder field. A colleague's DNS query times out.

Try answering in your own words: ① Can you treat 192.0.2.10 as the coffee shop's exclusive origin server? ② Can you treat the registrar as the website owner? ③ Can a timeout establish that the name does not exist? ④ What query conditions must you add so someone else can recheck your report?
This checks understanding and does not require interacting with third-party targets. A reference answer is a learning aid, not evidence that a learner has mastered the concept.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: A CDN address does not prove the origin server
paragraphs: No. An A record shows the address returned by this lookup; a CDN can proxy multiple websites. There is insufficient evidence that this address is exclusive to the coffee shop. It certainly does not place the entire CDN within the authorized testing scope.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Different roles are not interchangeable
paragraphs: No. A registrar provides domain registration services and is not necessarily the website operator. If holder information is not public, record that public information is insufficient; do not guess a name or ownership.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: A timeout does not mean nonexistence
paragraphs: No. A timeout means a response did not arrive in time, possibly because of network or service conditions. NXDOMAIN is the response status stating that the queried name does not exist. Even when receiving NXDOMAIN, retain the source, time, and query conditions.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: Let someone else repeat the check under known conditions
paragraphs: At minimum, retain the authorized scope, query date and time zone, source or resolver, network viewpoint, complete name, record type, response status, and original values. Include TTL when available, and separate observations from ownership that remains unverified.

sourceBody.text: 9 | Takeaway and sources

In one sentence: DNS describes how names connect to services, while WHOIS and RDAP describe roles in registration data. Both require sources, timestamps, and limitations before they become reliable asset clues.
The next unit is M02-05 Email Footprinting, connecting email clues with delivery paths and verifiable information. We do not add that second unit here.

Primary references: [DNS concepts, RFC 1034](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1034), [DNS records, RFC 1035](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1035), [IPv6 DNS, RFC 3596](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3596), [Negative caching, RFC 2308](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2308), [RDAP JSON, RFC 9083](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9083), [ICANN RDAP](https://www.icann.org/rdap), and [DNSSEC, RFC 4033](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4033).
